entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE-ZIMPOL V-band degree of linear polarisation, 3 December 2024 (ESO Phase 3 collection BETELGEUSE-B)
entries.finding: The ancillary degree-of-linear-polarisation map released beside the V-band intensity resolves patches of scattered light from one to about 4.5 stellar radii, which Kervella et al. 2016 and the release paper attribute to dust. Its instrumental floor, measured between eight and twelve stellar radii on the map itself, is 0.55 percent, and the patches reach about 5 percent. The map is drawn as a plane-of-sky slab spread along the line of sight by the scattering-angle efficiency of polarised light, which is the convention of the papers that publish such maps; no depth was observed.

entries.subject: How a sky-plane map is given depth
entries.finding: The first version pushed the image backwards: every sky pixel was spread along the whole line of sight, weighted by the Rayleigh polarisation efficiency, which is the convention of the polarimetric papers but is an extrusion, not a shape. Reviewed against how this project builds Helix and M2-9, where a shape is inferred from the observations rather than extruded, the decision is to fit an envelope instead. The azimuthally averaged radial profile between one and six stellar radii is scored against three envelopes projected through the cube: a spherical shell of free radius and gaussian thickness, the steady outflow a constant mass-loss rate gives, and constant depth, which is what an extrusion assumes. Measured on the released degree map, against a profile whose own rms is 1.41e-2: the shell leaves 4.28e-3 at radius 3.50 stellar radii and gaussian thickness 1.20, the outflow leaves 6.23e-3 at r^-0.70, and constant depth leaves 6.94e-3. The shell is drawn, each sky column is spread along it and normalised so the column still reproduces its measured degree, and the author refuses to write the grid if the shell is not the best of the three. The envelope is symmetric in depth, so each patch appears both in front of the star and behind it; one image cannot separate them and none of this is a measurement of depth.

entries.subject: The 4 micrometre light outside the photosphere as a third dataset
entries.finding: The VLTI/MATISSE reconstruction that paints this star's sphere carries a fifth of its flux outside the published 42.45 milliarcsecond disc. On the sphere that light is a flat plate drawn behind the body, which is a billboard, so it was tested for a shape the same way the polarisation was. Measured on the released reconstruction: the light falls by a factor of 2.3 across the first beam beyond the limb, 3.0 across the second and 3.2 across the next two, where a gaussian of the 4 milliarcsecond beam would fall by orders of magnitude, and it flattens into a shoulder between 42 and 50 milliarcseconds, which a beam skirt cannot produce. It is therefore resolved emission and not the instrument. The disc and the first beam beyond it are excluded, because inside the disc the sphere is drawn and within one beam of it the light is the star's own edge smeared by that beam. Over the 1.19 to 2.36 stellar radii that remain, the envelope that best projects to the measured profile is a steeply falling one, density as r to the minus 7.95, leaving 2.99e-6 against 1.50e-5 for the constant depth an extrusion assumes and a profile whose own rms is 2.09e-5. Colour is the reconstruction's own heat scale, the one the sphere already carries, because this is the same quantity.

entries.subject: Depth from an ALMA line cube's velocities, instead of a shape fitted to a projection
entries.finding: Every other dataset in this package is a sky image given a shape. This one is a line cube. ALMA project 2022.A.00026.S observed Betelgeuse in band 6 from 3 to 27 August 2023, and its spectral window 27 carries SiO v=0 J=5-4 at 217.10498 GHz, the molecule silicate dust condenses from. The archive's 72 GB pipeline cube was cut through its SODA service and boxed 300 mas about the phase centre by tools/objects/source-authoring/betelgeuse-shell/reduce-alma-sio.mts, keeping 47 channels of 1.35 km/s; the pipeline subtracts the continuum before imaging, so only the residual, the median of 1738 line-free channels, is removed. Every position is measured from the star found in the same observation's continuum image, 102 mas from the phase centre (see sio-registration). Measured about it, the line absorbs against the star from -21.3 to +16.4 km/s about the star's velocity, deepest 23 mJy per beam. Outside the star's continuum footprint, moment masking (the cube smoothed by its beam and three channels, cut at five times its noise and grown by the smoothing) keeps 331 pixels within six stellar radii, 22 beams carrying 0.55 Jy km/s: a lopsided ring brightest 2.4 radii out, with its weight 1.2 radii toward position angle 122 degrees. The star's velocity, the flux-weighted mean of the ring, is 5.1 km/s LSRK. The flow's terminal speed is the blue edge of the absorption, as a P Cygni profile is read: 21.3 km/s, 22.0 with half a channel. Every channel of every pixel is placed on a spherical outflow at that speed, at depth s v / sqrt(u^2 - v^2); 99.6 percent of the ring's flux lands in the grid, the deepest 5.2 radii along the line of sight. The red side of the absorption is gas falling back in front of the star, which this outflow places as if it were leaving, so the depths are the model's, not measured ones. A first version took the phase centre for the star. It drew the bright side of this ring as a lone clump 3.3 radii to the south-west, tied it to the 2019 clump and built an expansion age on that; all of it is withdrawn (see sio-clump-identity).

entries.subject: Where the star is in the ALMA images
entries.finding: The ALMA archive references the line cube and the continuum image of this member to the observation's phase centre, and the phase centre is not the star. The pipeline subtracts the continuum before it images a cube, so the cube cannot say where the star is: the median of its line-free channels is flat noise, peaking at 0.47 mJy per beam seven radii from the phase centre. The member's continuum image, made with the same regular calibration, shows the star at 43.7 mJy per beam, 121 times its noise. The centroid of its half-maximum lies 84.9 mas west and 57.2 mas south of the phase centre, 102 mas or 4.8 stellar radii; the peak refined by a parabola lies 4.5 mas from it; the two images' reference points agree to 0.8 mas. The line cube checks it independently, because absorption needs the star's continuum behind the gas: the centroid of the SiO absorption falls 2.2 mas from the continuum star. The author measures both and fails if the continuum shows no clean star, if the absorption is not centred on it, or if the box cannot hold the volume about it.

entries.subject: SiO emission eight to fourteen stellar radii north of the star
entries.finding: Moment masking also keeps emission 8 to 14 stellar radii north of the star: 29 percent of the masked flux outside the star's footprint, separated from the ring by an empty gap at six to eight radii, at -9 to +4 km/s about the star's velocity, beside a continuum peak of 1.8 mJy per beam, 5.1 times the noise, 11 radii north of the star. The volume holds six radii, so it is not drawn. It may be circumstellar gas. It may also be an artefact of the bright star in images made without self-calibration, although the deepest negative in the continuum image is only three times its noise. The archive holds self-calibrated continuum images of this member but no self-calibrated cube.
entries.revisitWhen: A self-calibrated SiO cube of this member, or another epoch of the line, which would show whether the northern emission and its continuum peak persist.

entries.subject: Whether the 2023 SiO is the 2019 Great Dimming clump, moved
entries.finding: The question came from a registration error and does not arise. A first version took the ALMA phase centre for the star, saw a single SiO clump 3.3 stellar radii to the south-west, in the quarter of the Great Dimming clump, and asked whether the two were one structure. Measured from the star itself, found in the same observation's continuum 102 mas from the phase centre, the SiO is a lopsided ring around the star two to four radii out, heaviest to the east-south-east, and absorbing in front of it. Nothing in this package connects it to the 2019 clump, and nothing is placed on the assumption that it is.
entries.revisitWhen: A second ALMA epoch of the same line, which would show whether any part of the ring moves outward.

entries.subject: Where the star sits inside the 2024 polarisation map
entries.finding: The two released V-band products carry one WCS but are not pixel-aligned to each other, and a first version of this package did not notice. The intensity image puts the star at pixel (513.00, 429.09), agreed by its peak, its half-maximum silhouette centroid and its ten-percent centroid. The degree map instead marks the stellar disc by setting 93 pixels to exact zero, a disc of 0.93 stellar radii centred at (502.40, 428.43); nothing else in that frame is exactly zero. The centres are 10.6 pixels apart, 38 mas, 1.8 stellar radii. Sampling the degree map about the intensity centre put the whole polarised envelope nearly two stellar radii off the star, which is visible in the render as the star standing outside its own cavity. Each product is now read about its own centre, and the author fails if the degree map marks no disc or marks one that is not about one stellar radius across. Verified against the publishers' own Fig. B.1, which is shipped in this package: its axis ticks calibrate the panel at 0.31348 mas per pixel with no assumption, its red circle is 21.0 mas in radius against this package's 21.15, and fitting the panel to the degree map at that scale peaks at 0.798 normalised cross-correlation with the figure's origin at degree-map pixel (501.53, 430.31). The old sampling centre scores 0.282 against that fit and the new one 0.771, 0.35 stellar radii from the paper's marker. The same fit settles the grid's handedness: the mirrored alternatives reach only 0.455 and 0.421, so increasing image column is west, as the sampling assumes.

entries.subject: How to colour a map of a dimensionless ratio in a volume
entries.finding: The first draft drew the degree of linear polarisation as white light on a zero-to-0.05 stretch, which read as a featureless pale smudge and threw away the structure the publishers show. The decision is to carry their own transfer function instead: matplotlib inferno on the zero-to-0.10 scale of the colourbar in Montarges et al. 2026 Fig. B.1, so the dataset is that figure given depth rather than an impression of it. Four stops of the bar, sampled at its quarters, are carried as four emission channels with the stop colours; the slab compiler sums emission along a ray, so tent weights over those stops interpolate the bar and a column emits the bar colour of its own measured degree. Every channel shares one depth profile, so a column's chromaticity does not vary along it, which is the condition under which the compositor's telescoping is exact rather than approximate. Four stops are the most an RGBA8 grid can carry. Two honest departures from the print are recorded: the renderer's exponential brightness transfer puts mid-scale values above a linear bar, and the instrumental floor measured beyond eight radii is subtracted here and is not in the figure, so empty sky is darker. The hue at every value is the published one, and the dataset is marked false colour and carries the bar as its legend.

entries.subject: The December 2019 RADMC-3D dust clump of Montargès et al. 2021, Nature 594, 365
entries.finding: Extended Data Table 3 publishes the optimised December 2019 solution in full: a sphere of radius 6.5 au centred at (-1.9, -3.0, +12.5) au, of constant dust density 3.2e-19 g/cm3 in MgFeSiO4 grains centred on 0.21 micrometres, in the coordinate system Extended Data Figure 6 defines as right ascension, declination and toward Earth. Those numbers place the clump south and slightly west of the star and between it and us, which is the hemisphere that dimmed. The au are given at the 222 pc the paper adopts, so this package reads them as angles at that distance and converts the angles to its own stellar radii: a sphere 1.38 radii in radius, centred 2.77 radii from the star. A first version divided by this scene's au per radius at 168 pc instead, which drew the clump 1.32 times too far out and too large. It is drawn as starlight scattered by that dust; the published density is uniform, so only the illumination varies across it. The January and March 2020 solutions in the same table are recorded by the authors as unoptimised best guesses and are not shipped.

entries.subject: The N_I pair of the same ESO release
entries.finding: The N_I degree map carries three times the polarised signal of the V map, but it sits in a tight ring at the limb, which is what a resolved disc's own edge produces, rather than in the envelope one to 4.5 radii out. Measured on the released products, in the ring one to 1.5 stellar radii out the mean degree is 0.037 against 0.014 for V, and inside half a radius 0.048 against 0.028; beyond about five radii both fall to their instrumental floor near 0.008.
entries.revisitWhen: A published separation of the limb polarisation from the envelope in this filter, or a deeper N_I epoch.

entries.subject: Drawing the clump as extinction of the photosphere rather than as scattered light
entries.finding: The clump is optically thick enough in the visible to dim the star, which is what the Great Dimming was, and the renderer can express that without per-pixel intersection. The slab compiler already takes absorption channels beside emission, and a leaf whose alpha is its extinction and whose colour is the light it scatters composites in ordinary source-over as transmission times what is behind plus the scattered term. Because every voxel of this clump stands clear of the photosphere in depth, ordering it in front of the detail scene is exact, so the star behind it is dimmed rather than covered. The absorption strength is set from the paper's own report that the southern hemisphere went ten times darker: the line of sight through the clump's centre carries an optical depth of ln 10, and the sum of the compiler's step lengths across the sphere is its diameter, so the strength is ln 10 divided by 13 au. The scattered light is drawn at four percent of the photosphere's surface brightness, which is a stated display level.

entries.subject: Whether a cloud that surrounds a body is a place of its own
entries.finding: It is not. A first draft shipped this package with its own catalogue entry, which put the dust on the map as a second destination beside the star it surrounds, reachable and framable on its own. The decision is that a volume that accompanies a body carries no place: the delivery names the body it attaches to, ships no catalogue entry, and its bank stays dark until one of that body's datasets asks for it. Betelgeuse's Datasets list holds all three entries, the two dust datasets borrow the MATISSE dataset's prepared surface for the star so they add no textures of their own, and one cloud lens is drawn at a time. Checked on the running application on 18 September 2026: the 2024 shell draws around the star, the 2019 clump draws in front of it and dims it, and the MATISSE dataset draws no cloud.

entries.subject: Whether the world camera draws celestial east on the side of the star the sky puts it
entries.finding: The grid is right: its axes are read from the products' own WCS, where increasing column is west and increasing row is north, and its sky plane reproduces the published figure's patch layout (Montarges et al. 2026, Fig. B.1) with east on the left; the mirrored fits to that figure score 0.455 and 0.421 against 0.798. The rendered frame is now checked too. Betelgeuse's default view is pinned by its default-view test with celestial north 42 degrees counterclockwise of screen-right and east 90 degrees beyond it. Rendered headless at that view on 18 September 2026, the light the SiO dataset adds over the MATISSE dataset lies at 147 degrees, 1.4 disc radii out, where the ring's east-south-east weight predicts 164 and a mirrored volume would put it at 280. Every lens of this package shares one bank frame, so the check covers them all. An earlier reading of the capture camera's east axis to the screen's right was made at a saved world camera of unknown roll, before the world-handedness fix.

entries.subject: Whether a public ALMA line cube can measure the depth this package infers
entries.finding: The envelope drawn here is a shape fitted to one projection, so it cannot say at what radius a patch really sits or which side of the star it is on. A spectral line cube can: the Doppler sign separates near from far and a velocity law turns the shift into a radius. Screened the ALMA archive within 0.02 degrees of this object's scene origin on 2026-09-18, 302 public rows in six projects, against this package's own geometry, a shell 148 milliarcseconds across inside an envelope reaching 190. Scored on the resolution each observation actually has, capped by its own maximum recoverable scale. Three projects are compact-configuration monitoring with beams of 3.5 to 3.8 arcseconds, 0.04 beams across the shell, and measure the star as a point: 2019.2.00120.S, 2019.A.00028.S and 2021.1.00927.S are out. 2019.1.01098.S reaches 35 mas in band 4 with SiO v=0 3-2, 4.2 beams across, recoverable to 667 mas, usable but coarse. 2015.1.00206.S reaches 16.8 mas in band 7 with CO 3-2, 8.8 beams across, recoverable to 302 mas, observed November 2015. The best is 2022.A.00026.S of August 2023: band 6 at 21.9 mas gives 6.8 beams across with CO 2-1 and SiO v=0, v=1 and v=2 5-4 and recovers to 351 mas, and band 7 at 14.2 mas gives 10.4 beams with CO 3-2 but recovers only to 200 mas. Its band 8 is the finest beam ever taken of this star at 9.7 mas and is rejected outright: it recovers only 127 mas and would throw the envelope away, which is exactly what the resolution rule exists to catch. Acted on in lens-sio-2023, from the band 6 SiO v=0 J=5-4 pipeline cube of 2022.A.00026.S, cut out through the archive's SODA service rather than restored from visibilities. Two limits stand. The cube is August 2023 and the polarisation map December 2024, so the line cube cannot place the 2024 patches. Carbon monoxide was not used, because in the inner envelope it is optically thick with rising and falling gas together and its velocity is not single-valued in radius.
